# Independent COMMENT review - PR 577

Candidate: `723e2d2ac6783b2cfe2fea78cacd2fc6b0088874` (clean worktree
`/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-574-merge-title-lean-code-lines`).
Trusted published-main policy/comparison: `c168340f5001d4a65304e90d2422a521de4157d5`.
Merge base: `92b252ed4bb1860b12a0a6c96084512f53ae9e10`.

Code verdict: **CHANGES_REQUESTED**. Prose verdict: **APPROVED** on the changed
protocol text as prose; its unconditional counting description depends on F1.
No blueprint or Lean declaration was changed, so mathematical-equivalence and
Lean-docstring prose checks have no changed target.

## Findings
- [ ] F1 (changes) `local/bin/pr_merge.py:684` - A valid multiline Lean string containing `/-` causes the scanner to suppress all subsequent code lines, so an actual theorem edit can be reported as `[lean 0]`. For example, both sides can start with `def s : String := "hello` followed by `/-"` on the next physical line, then change only `theorem t : True := trivial` to `theorem t : True := by trivial`. Lean accepts the multiline string (standalone `lake env lean --stdin` exited 0), but `lean_code_line_mask` yields `[True, False, False]`: the reset of `in_string` lets the literal `/-` open a block comment that never closes. This is more than an approximate classification of a string-content line: it hides an arbitrary suffix of real Lean declarations from the size signal. Fix: keep ordinary double-quoted string/escape state across physical lines until its closing quote, and add a focused delta regression for a later changed code line after such a literal.

## Review
The first-round PR patch is four files, 312 additions and 28 deletions. The
scanner otherwise handles the requested nested block/doc/module comments,
line comments, blank lines and same-line code with trailing comments. The raw
`-z` record walk handles the usual single- and double-path statuses; blob masks
are taken separately from the base and head; `-U0` hunk positions select only
changed physical lines. The unchanged `lean_line_delta` API wraps measurement
exceptions as `None`, and the existing post-gate subject/REST fallback remains
outside merge authority. The tests cover modified, added, deleted and renamed
Lean files, but not F1. The protocol amendment has a dated owner-issue trigger
and keeps the cosmetic subject contract; fix F1 without changing gates or
transport. The issue permits a simple approximate lexer; this finding concerns
its false classification of *later ordinary code*, not a demand for a complete
Lean parser. Exotic literals and malformed Lean syntax were not exhaustively
assessed.

Direct pinned-main tree comparison also lists telemetry paths missing from the
older branch. They are base-side changes since the merge base, not deletions in
this PR patch; MAIN reported its separate exact-head freshness admission.

## Checks And Limits
- Read issue #574 and PR #577 body through primary `local/bin/gh_common.py`; PR API reported the exact head, one commit, four changed files, and no prior review. Read trusted-ref reviewer personas, both code/prose prompt pairs, CONTRIBUTING section 5, review/meta/issues protocols, and the full PR diff and changed-file context.
- Git confirmed the candidate head and clean worktree; `git diff --check` passed on the four-file patch. `local-ci/build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`, `blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`, `statement-origin` and `summary` were all `success` on that SHA when read. PR body reports 643 unit tests, 9 skipped; not rerun here.
- Read MAIN's existing rooted `blueprint-leanok-axioms.log`: PASS 1610, FAIL 0, WARN 4 (all statement-only). No new full build, CI, render, rooted audit, real merge gate, or publication. The only fresh probe was the standalone multiline Lean parse and `lean_code_line_mask` result above; no end-to-end scratch-repository delta test was run.
